newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says Peru hostages at serious risk.
newsitem.headline: Germany says Peru hostages at serious risk.

text.p: Germany's foreign ministry said on Thursday the hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Peru had neither enough space to sleep nor enough food to eat.

Spokesman Martin Erdmann told journalists that the over 400 captive diplomats, businessmen and government officials were in a precarious situation at the hands of terrorists determined to reach their goals.

He said German ambassador Heribert Woeckel, one of the diplomats released on Wednesday to help negotiations between the Lima government and the leftwing guerrillas, had informed Bonn by telephone of the situation inside the residence.

"After more than 30 hours of captivity, in a psychologically difficult situation, there is not enough room to sleep, the sanitary situation is wanting and of course the provisions are insufficient for so many people in such a crowded area.
He called the situation "precarious" because, as Woeckel reported, "the hostage takers made a very calm and reasonable impression, but they also knew exactly what they want.

"They made a very determined impression. They're completely clear about their goals and want to reach these goals, that is, the release of their comrades from Peruvian, Columbian and Bolivian prisons."
"So the situation is serious. This is not a crime story that will certainly have a happy ending."
